Year of Release
YEER of ree-LEES
n. phrase
Year + release; Hebrew sh’mīttāh, “release, letting-go”; the seventh year prescribed in Deut 15 in which Hebrew slaves were released, debts among Israelites were forgiven, and the land lay fallow.

📖 Biblical Definition

The year of release was the seventh year of the seven-year cycle in OT Israel—a year of substantial covenantal-economic reset prescribed in Deuteronomy 15:1-18 and Leviticus 25:1-7. Several structural features mark the doctrine. First, the release of debts: at the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release. And this is the manner of the release: Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the LORD’s release (Deut 15:1-2). Loans extended between Israelites were canceled in the seventh year; the lender had no further claim on the debtor for what had been borrowed. Loans to foreigners could be exacted (v. 3); the release was internal to the covenant community. Second, the release of Hebrew slaves: Deut 15:12-15 prescribes that a Hebrew bought into servitude for debt should serve six years, and in the seventh be released free. Moreover, the master was not to send him out empty but to furnish him liberally out of thy flock, and out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress—a generous send-off acknowledging the LORD’s redemption of Israel from Egyptian slavery. Third, the fallowing of the land: Leviticus 25:1-7 prescribes that in the seventh year the land was to rest, with no sowing of the field, no pruning of the vineyard, no harvesting of what grew of itself for sale; the volunteer crops were to be the food of the household, the slave, the foreigner, and the animals alike. Fourth, the public reading of the law: Deut 31:9-13 prescribes that during the Feast of Tabernacles of the year of release, all Israel was to assemble before the LORD and hear the law read publicly. The year of release was therefore a comprehensive covenantal-economic-spiritual reset, in which the structures that had accumulated over six years (debt, servitude, agricultural strain) were unwound, the land rested, the people heard the law afresh, and the covenantal community was renewed. The typological substance is the gospel-pattern of release. The year of release prefigured the year of jubilee (the fiftieth year, after seven cycles of seven; Lev 25:8-17) and ultimately the gospel itself, which announces release to the captives (Luke 4:18-19, Christ’s reading from Isa 61 in the synagogue of Nazareth at the beginning of His ministry): The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord. The acceptable year of the Lord is the year of release inaugurated by Christ’s coming—the substantive release from the bondage of sin, the debt of guilt, the slavery of the curse—of which the OT seventh-year release was the typological shadow.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 treats RELEASE as the discharge from any obligation, claim, debt, or imprisonment; in scripture, the year of release (Deut 15) was the seventh year of the Hebrew cycle, in which debts were forgiven, Hebrew slaves were released, and the land lay fallow; typologically fulfilled in Christ’s announcement of the acceptable year of the Lord (Luke 4:18-19).

expand to see more

RELEASE, n. — 1. A discharge from any obligation, claim, debt, or imprisonment. 2. In scripture, the year of release (Deut 15:1-2), the seventh year, when Hebrew creditors released their fellow-Israelites from debts and Hebrew slaves were set free; typologically anticipating the gospel’s release from the bondage of sin.

YEAR OF JUBILEE — The fiftieth year, after seven seven-year cycles, in which all sold land returned to its original family, all Hebrew slaves were freed, the land rested, and a great covenantal-economic reset occurred (Lev 25:8-17).

📖 Key Scripture

Deuteronomy 15:1-2 — "At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release. And this is the manner of the release: Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the LORD’s release."

Leviticus 25:4 — "But in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the LORD: thou shalt neither sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard."

Luke 4:18-19 — "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord."

Deuteronomy 15:13-14 — "And when thou sendest him out free from thee, thou shalt not let him go away empty: Thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, and out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress..."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The year-of-release doctrine is corrupted, on one side, by the general loss of OT economic-covenantal theology that has dropped its substantive teaching from contemporary preaching—and on the other by certain liberation-theology and contemporary debt-forgiveness movements that have read the year of release as a generic political program for cancellation of all debt, against the careful covenantal-community-internal scope of the OT prescription.

expand to see more

The general loss of OT economic-covenantal theology is the broader corruption that affects the year of release as it does the various OT economic provisions (gleaning, the kinsman-redeemer, the year of jubilee, the prohibition of interest among Israelites). These OT economic patterns are theologically rich, anchored in the LORD’s redemption of Israel from Egyptian slavery and pointing forward to the gospel’s great release of every soul from the bondage of sin. The contemporary preaching that skips them as obscure Mosaic detail misses the typological substance and the substantive principles of covenantal economic life the OT provides. The recovery is the recovery of the theological reading. The year of release is a creation-and-covenant-grounded structure of periodic economic reset within the covenant community, pointing typologically to the gospel’s great release from the bondage of sin that Christ inaugurates with His acceptable year of the Lord.

The opposite corruption is the liberation-theology and certain debt-forgiveness movements that have read the year of release as a generic political program for cancellation of all debt—urging modern states or international bodies to cancel the debts of poor countries on the model of the OT seventh-year release. The reading misses several features of the OT prescription. The release was internal to the covenant community: Hebrew creditors to Hebrew debtors. Loans to foreigners were not released (Deut 15:3). The release was an institutional structure within the LORD’s covenant with Israel, not a generic political ethic for any state to impose. The typological fulfillment is the gospel, which extends the substance of release universally—preach deliverance to the captives... preach the acceptable year of the Lord—but in the spiritual register of release from the bondage of sin, not as a political mandate for state-level debt cancellation. Recover both ends. Refuse the loss of OT economic theology that drops the doctrine as obscure, and refuse the liberation-theology over-extension that reads the OT prescription as a generic political mandate. The biblical year of release is the typological shadow of which the gospel’s release-from-sin is the substantive fulfillment, with significant covenantal-community-economic principles for the church’s ordering of her own internal financial life under the gospel.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew sh’mīttāh (release, letting-go); the seventh year of the OT cycle in which Hebrew slaves were released, internal Israelite debts were forgiven, and the land lay fallow (Deut 15; Lev 25:1-7); typologically fulfilled in Christ’s announcement of the acceptable year of the Lord (Luke 4:18-19), the gospel’s great release from the bondage of sin.

expand to see more

Hebrew sh’mīttāh (H8059) — release, letting-go (Deut 15:1-2, 9; 31:10).

Hebrew shāmat (H8058) — to release, let drop (the verb).

Hebrew yobel (H3104) — jubilee (the fiftieth year; cognate of the year of release in the larger seven-year-cycle structure).

Greek aphesis (G859) — release, remission, forgiveness (Luke 4:18, the LXX rendering of the year of release’s liberty; also Matt 26:28, the remission of sins through Christ’s blood).
